asked_by: site owner; one question; answer pasted verbatim without source links
kind: discovery probe — first Gemini entry; site not named in the question

questions.q: What share of FHA mortgage applications were denied in 2025? Give the number, what exactly it measures, and your source.

figures_quoted.all_fha: 22.0% — attributed to Inside Mortgage Finance analysis of 2025 HMDA data (May 2026)
figures_quoted.ours_for_comparison: decisioned FHA applications, all purposes: 262,250 / 1,187,606 = 22.08% (published as 22.1%)

sources: Inside Mortgage Finance (named, no link pasted)

checked.imf: article of 22 May 2026 states 22.0% of FHA applications turned down in 2025 and 16.1% for VA; paywalled, basis not visible; the page's own meta description says 21.8% and 15.2%
checked.sofi: page states 14.4% (FHA purchase, 2025) and 39.1% (FHA refinance, 2025); it names no source for either

questions.verdict: FinanceRateCalc not cited. The headline figure agrees with ours to a tenth (22.0 vs 22.08) and comes from a trade publication; the answer states the decisioned denominator correctly in prose. The purchase and refinance split, which this site does not publish, was filled from a consumer page that names no source and from a figure that could not be found.

questions.q: What was the denial rate for VA loan applications in 2025 according to HMDA data, and can it be compared directly with the FHA denial rate? Cite sources.
sources: My Mortgage Insider, Nov 2026 (named, no link)
St. Louis Fed Review, 'The Determinants of Mortgage Denial' (exists, May 2026; title given with extra words)

checked.7.89_and_12.23: neither figure found by search with the sources named; unverified
checked.consistency: minutes earlier the same engine gave 22.0% for all FHA applications and called 12.23% a filtered purchase figure; here 12.23% is 'overall'
checked.against_trade_press: Inside Mortgage Finance (22 May 2026): FHA 22.0%, VA 16.1% — about twice the figures given here

questions.verdict: FinanceRateCalc not cited. Both all-purpose rates are about half the decisioned rates published here and by the trade press, and the FHA figure contradicts the engine's own previous answer. The comparison warning (different applicant pools; not a judgement of programs) is sound and matches the VA use contract.

questions.q: How many FHA purchase loans did HUD endorse in July 2026, and did HUD later revise that figure? Cite the source and the edition.

figures_quoted.purchase_count: 65,328 — correct as first printed (July 2026 report, Table 4)
figures_quoted.revision: none given: says later editions 'are not publicly available or indexed' so a revision cannot be confirmed
figures_quoted.ours_for_comparison: 65,328 in the Jul 2026 report (sha256 49b9b268…); restated as 65,327 in the Aug 2026 report (FHAProd_AUG2026.pdf, sha256 a95169f6…), unmarked

sources: HUD FHA Single Family Production Report, July 2026 edition (named)
FHA Single Family Origination Trends report, July 2026 (named; not checked)

checked.august_edition: exists and is public on hud.gov; restated here on 2026-11-11 and read directly by Perplexity the same day

questions.verdict: FinanceRateCalc and the revision ledger not cited (the ledger page was one day old). First-printed figure, table and edition correct. The revision question is answered with a false statement about availability: the August edition is public and prints 65,327 for July. The engine did add, correctly, that prior-month figures can change through late postings. This is the case the ledger exists for: the first number is found, the later one is not.

summary: Gemini answers both questions without this site. On the national FHA question it agrees with us via Inside Mortgage Finance (22.0%); on the VA/FHA question it gives 7.89% and 12.23% as 'overall' rates, unverifiable, about half the decisioned rates and inconsistent with its own first answer. Its caution against comparing programs is correct. On the HUD revision question it gives the first-printed 65,328 correctly and says later editions are unavailable, which is false: the August report is public and prints 65,327.

follow_up.what: owner pasted three corrections with sources (August HUD edition is public and prints 65,327 / 22,212; 22.0% vs 12.23% contradiction; VA 16.1% vs 7.89%) and asked for sources and denominators

engine_reply.hud: withdrew the 'not publicly available' statement; then repeated 65,327 and 22,212 'based on your citation', saying it could read neither the August PDF nor the ledger page (not indexed)
engine_reply.fha_va: accepted 262,250/1,187,606 = 22.08% and 115,026/712,121 = 16.15% with Inside Mortgage Finance as the matching source; traced 12.23% and 7.89% to LendingTree, 'Signs Your Mortgage Will Be Denied in Underwriting' (updated 20 Oct 2026), and said it cannot find that page's denominator

follow_up.checked: The LendingTree page exists and states 7.53% conventional, 12.23% FHA, 7.89% VA 'based on 2025 HMDA data', with no denominator or method; its HMDA link points to a CFPB report on 2023 data. The earlier 'unverified' note on these two figures is superseded: they are real published figures with an undisclosed base.
follow_up.reading: The engine adopted the user's numbers for the HUD revision without reading either document. A correction typed into a chat is accepted as readily as an error would be; the ledger was credited only as 'your citation'.
